en: Dhātukathā 2 Niddesa 2.5.
The Fifth Method: Exposition of Terms Not Included by What is Not Included.
Regarding the aggregates of form (*rūpakkhandha*), those phenomena which are not included by way of inclusion in the aggregates,

not included by way of inclusion in the bases (*āyatana*), and not included by way of inclusion in the elements (*dhātu*); and regarding those phenomena [in turn] which are not included by those [first] phenomena by way of inclusion in the aggregates,

not included by way of inclusion in the bases, and not included by way of inclusion in the elements— by how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are those phenomena not included?
Those states are not included within one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.
Those states which are with the aggregate of feeling … those states which are with the aggregate of perception …

Those phenomena which, by way of the aggregate of mental formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*), are not included in the inclusion of aggregates, not included in the inclusion of bases (*āyatana*), and not included in the inclusion of elements (*dhātu*)—
those phenomena [which are not included] by those phenomena … [and so on] … those phenomena are not included in two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements. Those phenomena which,
by way of the aggregate of consciousness (*viññāṇakkhandha*) … [and so on].
Those phenomena associated with the mind-base (manāyatana);
those phenomena associated with the eye-consciousness-element (cakkhuviññāṇadhātu); ... pe ...
those phenomena associated with the mind-element (manodhātu).
Those phenomena that are not included in the mind-consciousness element;

those phenomena that, by way of the mind faculty, are not included in the aggregate classification, not included in the base classification, and not included in the element classification; those phenomena [associated] with those [aforementioned] phenomena...
those phenomena are not included in four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
Those phenomena associated with the eye-base …pe… those phenomena associated with the tangible-object-base … those phenomena associated with the eye-element …pe…

Those phenomena which, in relation to the tangible element (*phoṭṭhabbadhātu*), are not included in the aggregate-grouping, not included in the base-grouping, and not included in the element-grouping—those phenomena [in relation] to those phenomena ... [as before] ...
those phenomena are not included in four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Those phenomena which, in relation to the mental-object base (*dhammāyatana*) ...

Those phenomena that are associated with the element of phenomena (*dhammadhātu*) … those phenomena that are associated with the female faculty (*itthindriya*) … those phenomena that are associated with the male faculty (*purisindriya*) …
Those phenomena which, by way of the life-faculty, are not included in the aggregate-grouping, not included in the base-grouping, and not included in the element-grouping—
those phenomena [in relation] to those phenomena … [and so on] … those phenomena are not included in one aggregate, one base, and seven elements. Those phenomena which,
by way of the truth of origination … [and so on].

Those phenomena that are not included in the aggregate-grouping, not included in the base-grouping, and not included in the element-grouping by way of the truth of the path, and those phenomena that are not included [in the same groupings] by way of the truth of cessation—
those phenomena [are] not included in two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

Those phenomena which are not included by the eye-faculty …pe… those phenomena which are not included by the body-faculty, being neither included by the aggregate-inclusion, nor included by the base-inclusion, nor included by the element-inclusion—
those phenomena [in turn] have other phenomena …pe… those phenomena are not included by four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Those phenomena associated with the faculty of pleasure … those phenomena associated with the faculty of pain … those phenomena associated with the faculty of mental joy …
The states associated with the faculty of mental distress … the states associated with the faculty of equanimity … the states associated with the faculty of faith …
Those phenomena [associated] with the faculty of energy … those phenomena [associated] with the faculty of mindfulness … those phenomena [associated] with the faculty of concentration …
Those phenomena by means of the faculty of wisdom … those phenomena by means of the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" … those phenomena by means of the faculty of final knowledge …
Those phenomena which, by way of the faculty of one who has final knowledge (*aññātāvindriya*), ...
those phenomena which, by way of ignorance (*avijjā*) ...

those phenomena which, by way of volitional formations conditioned by ignorance (*avijjāpaccayā saṅkhāra*), are not included in the classification of aggregates (*khandha-saṅgaha*), not included in the classification of bases (*āyatana-saṅgaha*), and not included in the classification of elements (*dhātu-saṅgaha*); those phenomena [which are] with respect to those phenomena ... pe ... [as before].
Those phenomena are not included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements. Those phenomena which,

by way of the condition of volitional formations (*saṅkhāra-paccaya*), are not included within the aggregate-inclusion, not included within the base-inclusion, and not included within the element-inclusion—
those phenomena [in turn] are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.

With consciousness as condition, by way of name-and-form, those phenomena which are not included in the aggregate-grouping, not included in the base-grouping, and not included in the element-grouping— and those phenomena [conditioned] by those phenomena … [and so on] … those phenomena are not included in one aggregate,

one base, and seven elements. With name-and-form as condition, by way of the sixfold base, those phenomena which are not included in the aggregate-grouping, not included in the base-grouping, and not included in the element-grouping— and those phenomena [conditioned] by those phenomena … [and so on] … [those phenomena are not included in one aggregate, one base, and seven elements].
Those states are not included within three aggregates, one base, and one element.
Those states which, by way of the condition of the sixfold base, [arise] through contact;
those states which, by way of the condition of contact, [arise] through feeling...
Those phenomena which, with feeling as condition, [arise] through craving;
those phenomena which, with craving as condition, [arise] through clinging;

those phenomena which, through kamma-existence, are not included in the classification of aggregates, not included in the classification of bases, and not included in the classification of elements—those phenomena which [in turn arise] through those phenomena ... [and so on].
Those phenomena are not included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Those phenomena belonging to the formless existence (arūpabhava) … those phenomena belonging to the neither-perception-nor-non-perception existence (nevasaññānāsaññābhava) …
Those phenomena that are included by way of fourfold existence (*catuvokārabhava*)—
those phenomena which, by way of the bases of psychic power (*iddhipāda*), are not included in the aggregate-inclusion, not included in the base-inclusion, and not included in the element-inclusion—
and those phenomena [associated] with them: those phenomena are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena that exist through non-percipient existence;
those phenomena that exist through one-constituent existence;
those phenomena that exist through birth...
Those phenomena which, by way of aging...

by way of death, are not included in the classification of aggregates (*khandha-saṅgaha*), not included in the classification of bases (*āyatana-saṅgaha*), and not included in the classification of elements (*dhātu-saṅgaha*); those phenomena which [are related] to those [other] phenomena...
[and so on]... those phenomena are not included in one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.

Those phenomena which, by way of lamentation (*parideva*), are not included in the aggregate-grouping (*khandha-saṅgaha*), are not included in the sense-base grouping (*āyatana-saṅgaha*), and are not included in the element grouping (*dhātu-saṅgaha*)— those phenomena [in relation] to which other phenomena [are not included] … [as before] … those phenomena are not included in four aggregates,
two sense-bases, and eight elements. Those phenomena which, by way of sorrow (*soka*) … [as before] … are not included in four aggregates, two sense-bases, and eight elements.
Those phenomena that [arise] through suffering… those phenomena that [arise] through mental distress… those phenomena that [arise] through despair…
The qualities that are developed by means of the foundations of mindfulness...
the qualities that are developed by means of the right efforts...
the qualities that are developed by means of the meditative absorptions...
Those phenomena associated with the immeasurables … those phenomena associated with the five faculties … those phenomena associated with the five powers …
The states that [arise] through the seven factors of enlightenment...
the states that [arise] through the noble eightfold path...
the states that [arise] through contact...
Those phenomena that belong to feeling … those phenomena that belong to perception … those phenomena that belong to volition …
Those phenomena which are not included by resolution (*adhimokkha*)...

those phenomena which are not included by attention (*manasikāra*), and which are not included by the inclusion of aggregates (*khandha-saṅgaha*), nor included by the inclusion of bases (*āyatana-saṅgaha*), nor included by the inclusion of elements (*dhātu-saṅgaha*); those phenomena [which are not included] by those [respective factors]...
those phenomena are not included by two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

Those phenomena which, by way of the inclusion of aggregates (*khandha-saṅgaha*), are not included [in the aggregate of consciousness], and by way of the inclusion of bases (*āyatana-saṅgaha*) and elements (*dhātu-saṅgaha*), are not included [in the base of mind or the element of consciousness];
those phenomena which [are not included] by those [other] phenomena … [and so on] … those phenomena are not included in four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
2.5.1. Triads (*tika*).
Those states which [arise] with wholesome states;
those states which [arise] with unwholesome states;
those states which [arise] with states associated with pleasant feeling.
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena associated with painful feeling...
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling...
those phenomena which [arise] with resultant phenomena...
Those phenomena which [are related] to phenomena that are subject to maturation;
those phenomena which [are related] to phenomena that are neither clung-to nor conducive to clinging;
those phenomena which [are related] to phenomena that are defiled and subject to defilement.
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena that are undefiled and non-defiling...
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought...
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena without applied thought but with sustained thought alone...
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by rapture...
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by pleasure...
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by equanimity...
Those phenomena that [arise] together with phenomena to be abandoned by vision;
those phenomena that [arise] together with phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation;
those phenomena that [arise] together with phenomena rooted in what is to be abandoned by vision.
Those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation;
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena leading to accumulation;
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena leading to diminution.
Those phenomena which [arise] through the phenomena of the trainee;
those phenomena which [arise] through the phenomena of the one beyond training;
... those phenomena which [arise] through the exalted phenomena.
Those states which [arise] with immeasurable states as their objects...
those states which [arise] with limited objects as their objects...
those states which [arise] with exalted objects as their objects...
Those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena that have immeasurable objects;
those phenomena which [arise] through inferior phenomena;
those phenomena which [arise] through sublime phenomena.
Those states which [are associated with] states fixed in wrongness;
those states which [are associated with] states fixed in rightness;
those states which have the Path as their object.
Those phenomena that [arise] with phenomena having the Path as their cause...
those phenomena that [arise] with phenomena having the Path as their predominance...
(18) ...those phenomena that [arise] with phenomena having the past as their object...
Those states [conditioned] by states having future objects...
those states [conditioned] by states having present objects...
(20) those states [conditioned] by states having internal objects...

Those phenomena which, through external objects, or those phenomena which, through internal-and-external objects, are not included in the classification of aggregates (*khandha*), not included in the classification of bases (*āyatana*), and not included in the classification of elements (*dhātu*)—those phenomena [in relation] to those phenomena ... [and so forth] ...
those phenomena are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.

Those phenomena which are not included by way of the aggregate-inclusion, the base-inclusion, or the element-inclusion with respect to phenomena that are visible and impinging, or with respect to phenomena that are invisible and impinging—those phenomena [are related] to those phenomena... [and so on] ...
those phenomena are not included by four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
The Group on Roots (Hetu-gocchaka):
Those phenomena which [arise] together with phenomena that are roots...
Those phenomena which, by way of the aggregates, are not included among those phenomena that are both roots and accompanied by roots;

and those phenomena which, by way of the aggregates, are not included among those phenomena that are both roots and associated with roots—those phenomena, by way of bases, are not included, and by way of elements, are not included.
Those phenomena [not included] by those [other] phenomena... [as above] ...are not included in two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Those phenomena [associated] with phenomena that have causes;
those phenomena [associated] with phenomena associated with causes;
those phenomena [associated] with phenomena that both have causes and are not themselves causes.
Those phenomena which, by way of the inclusion of aggregates (*khandha-saṅgaha*), are not included among those phenomena that are associated with roots but are not themselves roots;

and those phenomena which, by way of the inclusion of bases (*āyatana-saṅgaha*) and the inclusion of elements (*dhātu-saṅgaha*), are not included among those phenomena that are both with root and accompanied by root—
those phenomena [are] not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
2.5.2.2. Cūḷantaraduka (The Short Intermediate Dyads) Those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena that have no conditions...

those phenomena which [are associated] with unconditioned phenomena that are not included in the aggregate classification, not included in the base classification, and not included in the element classification—those phenomena which [are associated] with those phenomena... pe...
Those phenomena are not included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

Those phenomena which are not included by way of aggregate-inclusion, base-inclusion, and element-inclusion among those phenomena that are visible (*sanidassana*)... among those phenomena that are impinging (*sappaṭigha*)... [and so forth]. Among those phenomena, those phenomena which... [and so forth].

Those phenomena are not included within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements. As for those phenomena which, among material phenomena, are not included by way of inclusion in the aggregates, not included by way of inclusion in the bases, and not included by way of inclusion in the elements—
those phenomena [in turn] are not included within one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.
Those phenomena which, by way of the inclusion of aggregates,

the inclusion of bases, and the inclusion of elements, are not included among immaterial phenomena... [and] those phenomena which, by way of the inclusion of aggregates, the inclusion of bases, and the inclusion of elements, are not included among supramundane phenomena—
those phenomena [in turn] are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
2.5.2.3. The Group on the Taints (Āsavagocchaka).
Those phenomena which [arise] from the taints;
those phenomena which [arise] from both the taints and the phenomena associated with the taints.

Those phenomena which, by way of the inclusion of aggregates (*khandha-saṅgaha*), are not included among the taints (*āsava*) nor among the phenomena associated with the taints, and which, by way of the inclusion of bases (*āyatana-saṅgaha*) and the inclusion of elements (*dhātu-saṅgaha*), are not included— those phenomena [in relation] to those phenomena … [and so on] … those phenomena are not included within two aggregates,
eleven bases, and seventeen elements. Those phenomena which, by way of the inclusion of aggregates,
are not included among the phenomena free from taints (*anāsava*) … [and so on].

Those phenomena which, by way of inclusion in the aggregates (*khandha*), are not included among the phenomena associated with the taints (*āsava*); those phenomena which, by way of inclusion in the aggregates, are not included among the phenomena both associated with the taints and themselves not being taints;

and those phenomena which, by way of inclusion in the aggregates, are not included among the phenomena dissociated from the taints and themselves free from taints (*anāsava*)—those phenomena, in relation to those [other] phenomena ... [and so forth].
Those states are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
2.5.2.4–10. The Group on Fetters (Saṃyojana-gocchaka), etc.:
Those states which [are associated] with the states that are fetters...
Those phenomena which [are related] to the phenomena of the scriptures;
those phenomena which [are related] to the phenomena of the floods;
those phenomena which [are related] to the phenomena of the yokes.
Those phenomena which, by way of the hindering phenomena...
by way of the defiling phenomena...

by way of both the defiling phenomena and those phenomena defiled by them, are not included in the classification of aggregates, not included in the classification of bases, and not included in the classification of elements—those phenomena, by way of those phenomena... [and so forth].
Those phenomena are not included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Those phenomena which [are associated] with non-clung-to phenomena...
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena associated with clinging...

Those phenomena which, by way of inclusion in aggregates, inclusion in bases, and inclusion in elements, are not included among those phenomena that are dissociated from the taints, are not adhered to, and possess objects—
those phenomena [are] not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena that [arise] with phenomena that are without objects;
those phenomena that [arise] with phenomena that are not consciousness;
those phenomena that [arise] with phenomena dissociated from consciousness.
Those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena associated with the mind;
those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena originated by the mind;
those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena coexistent with the mind.

Those phenomena which, by way of being concomitant with the mind, are not included in the same aggregate-grouping as those [other] phenomena; those phenomena which, by way of external phenomena, are not included in the same aggregate-grouping as those [other] phenomena;

those phenomena which, by way of derived phenomena, are not included in the same aggregate-grouping, nor included in the same sense-sphere-grouping, nor included in the same element-grouping as those [other] phenomena... [and so on].
Those phenomena are not included within one aggregate (khandha), one base (āyatana), and seven elements (dhātu).
Those phenomena which are not included within the aggregates, not included within the bases, and not included within the elements by way of inclusion among mental phenomena—
those phenomena [in relation] to those [other] phenomena … [and so on] … those phenomena are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
Those phenomena which [arise] through mental factors;
those phenomena which [arise] through states associated with consciousness;
those phenomena which [arise] through states conjoined with consciousness.

Those phenomena which, by way of being conjoined with and produced by the mind, are not included in the aggregate classification, not included in the base classification, and not included in the element classification— those phenomena, in relation to those [other] phenomena … [and so on] … those phenomena which,

by way of being conjoined with, produced by, co-existent with, and accompanying the mind, are not included in the aggregate classification, not included in the base classification, and not included in the element classification— those phenomena, in relation to those [other] phenomena … [and so on] …
Those phenomena are not included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.

Among internal phenomena, those phenomena which are not included by way of the inclusion of aggregates, not included by way of the inclusion of bases, and not included by way of the inclusion of elements—those phenomena [in relation to] those [other] phenomena ...
[and so on] ... those phenomena are not included within three aggregates, one base, and one element.
2.5.2.11–13. The Group on Clinging (Upādāna-gocchaka), etc.
Those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena of clinging … those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena of defilements …
Those phenomena which, by way of the aggregates, are not included among the defilements themselves nor among the phenomena associated with defilement;
those phenomena which, by way of the aggregates, are not included among the defilements themselves nor among the phenomena defiled by defilement;

those phenomena which, by way of the aggregates, are not included among the defilements themselves nor among the phenomena associated with defilement—those phenomena which, by way of the bases (*āyatana*) and the elements (*dhātu*), are likewise not included... [and so forth].
Those phenomena are not included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Regarding those phenomena that are associated with non-defiled phenomena...
regarding those phenomena that are associated with defiled phenomena...
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena associated with defilements;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena that are defiled but are not themselves defilements;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena that are both associated with defilements and are themselves defilements.
Those states which [are associated] with states dissociated from defilements and non-defiled;
those states which [are associated] with states to be abandoned by vision;
those states which [are associated] with states to be abandoned by cultivation.
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena whose causes are to be abandoned by vision;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena whose causes are to be abandoned by cultivation;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by applied thought (*savitakka*).
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by investigation;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by rapture;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena conjoined with rapture.
Those phenomena which [arise] with states accompanied by pleasure...
those phenomena which [arise] with states accompanied by equanimity...
those phenomena which [arise] with states not belonging to the sense sphere...
Those phenomena that [arise] with respect to form-sphere phenomena;
those phenomena that [arise] with respect to formless-sphere phenomena;
those phenomena that [arise] with respect to unincluded phenomena.
Those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena that lead to liberation;
those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena that are fixed;
those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena that are unsurpassed.
Regarding those states that are not included among the aggregates, not included among the bases,
and not included among the elements by way of inclusion through the states associated with the refuges—
by how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are those states not included?
Those states are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, or ten elements.
[Namely: matter, the mental-object base, the mental-object element, femininity, masculinity, life-faculty, and name-and-form.
The two types of existence, birth, aging,
and the form of death are without an object; they are not associated with consciousness, but are dissociated from consciousness and originate together with it.
Co-existent and revolving;
external, derived, two, object—this is the method for discerning the well-understood. [22]
The fifth [section] is the exposition of the uncomprised by means of the uncomprised.
